title: Represent a Fraction Greater Than One on a Number Line
goal: I can count fractional units beyond one and compare a fraction with one.
catchAll: Keep the denominator fixed as you pass one. A numerator larger than the denominator means more than one whole.

teacher.def: The denominator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are in the whole. It is the bottom part of the fraction
A unit fraction is ONE part of a whole. It always has a numerator of one.
The numerator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are being described. It is the top part of the fraction.
A fraction is a number used when a whole is split into equal parts.

glossary.whole: the one shape, unit length, complete piece or entire set named in the question
glossary.partition: divide a whole into equal parts
glossary.interval: the distance between neighboring marks on a number line

screens.title: Find one whole unit
text: The distance from 0 to 1 is one whole. This line keeps that same unit length from 1 to 2 and from 2 to 3.

screens.title: Split every unit equally
text: There are two equal gaps in 0 to 1. Each gap is one half-unit.
The highlighted first gap ends at 1/2. Zero is the start, not a gap.

screens.title: Reach one
text: Two half-unit gaps reach 1.
We can name that point 2/2 because two halves make one whole.

screens.title: Continue beyond one
text: Take one more gap of the SAME size.
The total from zero is now three half-unit gaps: 3/2. Do not restart the numerator at 1.

screens.title: The bottom still describes ONE unit
text: The entire line has several wholes, but the bottom stays 2.
Two equal gaps fit in each whole unit; drawing a longer line does not change their size.

screens.title: Compare with one
text: This point is 3/2. It lies to the right of 1.
It takes two halves to reach 1, and three halves go farther. So 3/2 is greater than one.

screens.title: Less than and equal to one
text: This point is 1/2, to the left of 1, because it uses fewer than two half-unit gaps.
The point 2/2 is exactly 1. Compare how many same-size gaps reach the point and how many make one whole.

screens.title: Continue through two and three
text: With thirds, three gaps reach 1, six reach 2, and nine reach 3.
This point uses eight third-sized gaps: 8/3 is more than 2 but less than 3.

screens.title: Compare with four whole units
text: With halves, eight gaps reach 4 whole units.
Seven half-unit gaps stop before 4. So 7/2 is less than 4, even though 7 is larger than 4.
